correctness.rationale: For every \(\alpha>2\), exact Pareto moments put the lower one-sigma endpoint strictly below the support edge, reducing the event to one CDF evaluation. The resulting exact formula is algebraic. Writing its tail exponent as the sum of two logarithms and applying \(\log(1+x)>x/(1+x)\) twice proves the strict exponent bound \(>2\) over the entire domain; the second strict step is equivalent to \((\alpha-1)^2>\alpha(\alpha-2)\). A direct Taylor expansion gives the stated endpoint limit and first correction. Finite numerical checks are supplementary only.

value.rationale: The one-standard-deviation central probability is an explicitly studied variation-comparison functional for classical distribution families. This result gives its complete sharp Pareto type-I classification throughout the finite-variance regime, including nonattainment and the first approach-to-extremality term. It also separates two opposite Pareto endpoints: shape near \(2\) makes tail-infimum anti-concentration vanish, while shape tending to infinity minimizes the central one-sigma mass. This is a natural family-wide invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
